finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole() returns a boolean that is discarded, so any authenticated caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe; the caller controls the tenant path parameter and the User roles passed to wipe().

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) receives caller identity and target tenant.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called; its boolean result is discarded, so no exception is thrown.
requireRole is a non-throwing predicate (Javadoc at line 13 states 'Does not throw').

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and does not enforce anything. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws SecurityException and is the working control; export (line 32) uses it correctly, wipe does not. No other guard exists in this file.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so its result is discarded and nothing aborts; checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws but is not called in wipe(). No other guard exists in the repo: the only other file-level matches are the wipe/checkRole/requireRole definitions and export at line 32, and no HTTP router or caller is present to add a check.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which only returns a boolean (src/Admin.java:14-16), so the result is discarded and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any caller holding any role, whereas export at src/Admin.java:32 correctly uses the throwing checkRole. The attacker is an authenticated low-privilege user, which is a real escalation; the repo contains no route handler, so the upstream authentication layer is unverified, but no control within the code blocks the call.

finding.claim: Neither wipe() nor export() checks that the caller belongs to or holds OWNER for the requested tenant, so an OWNER of one tenant may act on another tenant (cross-tenant IDOR/BOLA). Plausible; depends on code outside this repo.
finding.source: An authenticated user holding OWNER in some tenant supplies a different tenant ID in the path.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 and repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33.

trace.note: export(User u, String tenant) takes the tenant from the request.
checkRole(u, "OWNER") checks only the role name; the User record (line 4) has no tenant field, so it cannot scope the role to a tenant.
repo.export(tenant) runs for whichever tenant was requested.
wipe(User u, String tenant) has the same missing tenant-scope check before repo.wipe at line 27.

finding.guards_checked: No tenant-membership or tenant-ownership check exists in src/Admin.java. Enforcement, if any, may sit in the Repo implementation or HTTP layer, which are not in this repo and were not verified.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at line 26, so its result is discarded and wipe() has no role check at all. checkRole (lines 18-22) throws, and export() calls it at line 32, but it only tests the role name and has no tenant scope. No tenant-membership check exists anywhere in src/Admin.java. The Repo interface (lines 6-9) has no implementation in this repo.
verdict.reason: The trace misdescribes wipe(): src/Admin.java:26 is a discarded requireRole call, so the flaw there is a missing role check rather than a missing tenant check, and the cross-tenant claim for export() at lines 32-33 depends on a Repo implementation or HTTP layer (src/Admin.java:6-9) that is not in this repo and was not verified.
